metadata.topic: Nuclear Physics — Mass-Energy Equivalence: E = Δmc² for Rn-222 Alpha Decay
metadata.note: Masses given in paper: Rn-222=368.54918×10⁻²⁷ kg, Po=361.89489×10⁻²⁷ kg, alpha=6.64466×10⁻²⁷ kg. c=3.0×10⁸ m/s. Δm = 0.00963×10⁻²⁷ = 9.63×10⁻³⁰ kg. E = 9.63×10⁻³⁰ × (3×10⁸)² = 8.67×10⁻¹³ J. A and Z values (Q6b(ii)) are covered in PHY-JAN22-Q6bc_radon-decay.json. Half-life mass (Q6c(ii)) also in that file.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q6b(iii) — E=mc² Energy from Rn-222 Alpha Decay
question.text:
Radon-222 decays by alpha particle emission:

\({}^{222}_{86}\text{Rn} \rightarrow {}^{218}_{84}\text{Po} + {}^{4}_{2}\alpha\)

The masses of the nuclides are:

  • \({}^{222}_{86}\text{Rn} = 368.54918 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)
  • \({}^{218}_{84}\text{Po} = 361.89489 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)
  • \({}^{4}_{2}\alpha = 6.64466 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)

Use Einstein's mass-energy equation to calculate the energy released during this reaction. [c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹] (4 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Step 1 — Mass defect:
Δm = m(Rn) − m(Po) − m(α)
= (368.54918 − 361.89489 − 6.64466) × 10⁻²⁷
= 0.00963 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 9.63 × 10⁻³⁰ kg

Step 2 — Energy:
E = Δm × c² = 9.63 × 10⁻³⁰ × (3.0 × 10⁸)²
= 9.63 × 10⁻³⁰ × 9.0 × 10¹⁶
= 8.67 × 10⁻¹³ J

steps.label:
Given masses (×10⁻²⁷ kg): Rn-222 = 368.54918  |  Po-218 = 361.89489  |  alpha = 6.64466
Formula: Δm = m(reactants) − m(products)  |  E = Δm × c²  |  c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
Calculate the mass defect Δm. (2 marks)
Calculate the energy released E = Δmc². (2 marks)
